records.text: AI Voice Assistant Platform
Soft Debt Collection Calls
Technical & Commercial Proposal
Prepared for:  TBC Bank JSC
Submitted by:  LLC Loialte
RFI Reference:  0007249
Date:  30 July 2026
1. Executive Summary
Loialte proposes a production-oriented Georgian AI voice platform for outbound soft collections, integrated with TBC Bank's existing telephony and collections/CRM environment.

The solution is intentionally separated into a real-time voice layer, a conversational orchestration layer, and a deterministic policy-control layer. The language model supports understanding and controlled response drafting, but it does not decide customer eligibility, payment-plan terms, disclosure rights, or escalation outcomes. TBC systems remain the source of truth for customer, balance, policy and payment data.

The initial use case covers early-stage, pre-legal collection calls in Georgian: identity confirmation before disclosure; approved reminders; promise-to-pay capture; payment-date or installment discussion within Bank-defined rules; Bank-controlled SMS payment-link delivery; structured outcome write-back; and warm transfer or call termination for protected scenarios.
2. Understanding of the Requirement and Success Criteria

The RFI requires an AI/software layer only. TBC will continue to operate the dialer, carrier and telephony infrastructure. The vendor solution must connect through an approved SIP/media or API interface, retrieve only the minimum customer context required for the call, and write back structured outcomes in real time.

3.1 Included in the base implementation

One approved integration to TBC telephony through SIP/media or a documented API interface; no carrier, dialer or PSTN service supplied by Loialte.
One two-way collections/CRM integration for customer context, policy parameters, call status and outcome write-back.
One Bank-controlled SMS/payment-link API integration; TBC authorizes, creates and delivers the message/link through approved systems.
Identity gating, approved reminders, promise-to-pay, permitted payment-plan discussion, callbacks, escalation and termination logic.
Business-user configuration portal with SSO/MFA integration, RBAC, maker-checker approval, versioning, sandbox, effective dates and rollback.
Operational reporting, monitoring, support, incident management, SLA reporting, documentation and training.
Security/privacy design pack, subprocessor register, DPA/DPIA support, retention configuration and production-readiness evidence.
3.2 Explicit exclusions from the base price
TBC dialer, carrier/PSTN charges, telephone numbers, session border controller and core telephony operations.
SMS carrier fees, payment processing fees and any Bank-side license or infrastructure cost.
Voice biometric authentication, autonomous credit decisions, legal-collection activity and unapproved discount/settlement authority.
Full enterprise BI/data-warehouse implementation, inbound calling, additional languages or additional CRM/telephony integrations.
Material custom development outside the signed backlog and acceptance criteria; such changes follow the approved change-control process.
4. Proposed Technical Architecture

The production baseline excludes web-originated calling from the initial scope. Calls are placed and managed by TBC's existing telephony environment. The AI layer receives the approved audio stream through a secure SIP/media interface and returns synthesized audio through the same controlled boundary.

4.2 End-to-end data and call flow
TBC creates an approved campaign or call instruction using a customer reference and policy version; only minimum required data is exposed.
TBC telephony places the call and streams audio through the approved secure media interface.
The Georgian STT service transcribes the caller turn; number/date/currency normalization generates structured slots with confidence scores.
The orchestrator loads permitted customer context and requests an explicit policy decision before disclosure or negotiation.
The language model receives a constrained state, approved facts and response schema; unsupported free-form commitments are rejected.
Approved response text is synthesized and returned to the live call; barge-in stops playback and returns control to listening mode.
Events and final disposition are written to CRM using idempotency keys, retries and reconciliation; no outcome exists only in vendor logs.
For payment links, the platform invokes TBC's approved API. TBC generates/authorizes and sends the link; the vendor does not create payment credentials.
For escalation, the live call and a structured summary are transferred to the Bank's approved human queue where technically supported.
5. Conversation Design and Collections Controls
5.1 Identity and disclosure

The base scope uses Bank-approved knowledge-based or account-context verification; voice biometrics is excluded. The exact questions, retry count and lockout behavior are configured by TBC. Until verification succeeds, the assistant may identify the Bank and request the approved verification information, but it may not reveal balance, overdue status, creditor details, payment terms or other protected account information.
Verification inputs are normalized and checked by deterministic rules or Bank APIs, not accepted solely from LLM interpretation.
Low-confidence speech is repeated back or confirmed explicitly before it is used in a critical field.
Failed verification, wrong-party contact and third-party answers result in neutral closure without debt disclosure.
Every identity decision records policy version, input source, result, timestamp and reason code.

The Bank's CRM or policy service provides the eligible options for each customer. The AI assistant may explain and confirm those options, but it may not calculate a new discount, waive a fee, alter eligibility or extend a term. Each accepted promise is read back and confirmed before write-back.

records.text: 6.2 API behavior and error handling
Every call/session and outbound write uses a correlation ID; every write-back uses an idempotency key.
Transient errors use bounded exponential retry; permanent errors are routed to a dead-letter queue and surfaced to operations.
CRM reconciliation compares vendor events with Bank acknowledgments and reports unmatched outcomes.
Timeouts in identity, policy, customer-context or payment-link services trigger fail-closed behavior; protected information is not disclosed.
Schemas are versioned and backward-compatible during agreed migration periods; material changes require joint approval.
API secrets are stored in an approved secrets manager, rotated and never embedded in prompts, scripts or source code.

The proposed control set is designed for TBC due diligence and contractual approval; it does not assume that any third-party service is acceptable before the Bank completes its review.

8. Business-User Configurability and Change Governance

Routine campaign and script changes are managed through a controlled portal, without vendor engineering. Compliance-sensitive rules remain subject to maker-checker approval and cannot be promoted directly from draft to production by one user.

Every version stores author, approver, timestamp, effective period, linked test evidence and rollback target.

Emergency changes use a separate authorized path and require retrospective review on the next business day.
